# Job locations, as BigQuery answers. A job that names INFORMATION_SCHEMA regions of several
# locations runs in the US, and names a region of another location as a dataset of the project.
# https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/locations

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `region-eu`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA, `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA
=> error contains: :region-eu was not found in location US

# A single region does not match the multi-region it lies in.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA, `region-us-central1`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA
=> error contains: :region-us-central1 was not found in location US

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `region-nowhere`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA
=> error contains: Unrecognized region: nowhere

# The location CREATE SCHEMA names must be the job's, which a job that names no dataset has in the
# US.
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS scalars_locations_eu OPTIONS (location = 'EU');
SELECT 1
=> error contains: Location specified in query EU is not consistent with current execution region US

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS scalars_locations_nowhere OPTIONS (location = 'nowhere');
SELECT 1
=> error contains: Invalid location 'nowhere'

# ALTER SCHEMA takes no location, the dataset's own or another.
ALTER SCHEMA scalars SET OPTIONS (location = 'US')
=> error contains: Unknown option: location

ALTER SCHEMA scalars SET OPTIONS (location = 'EU')
=> error contains: Unknown option: location

# BigQuery reads a region qualifier whose prefix is not in lower case as a project ID, which it
# rejects.
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM `REGION-EU`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA
=> error contains: Invalid project ID 'REGION-EU'. Project IDs must contain 6-63 lowercase letters, digits, or dashes.
